title: Next: faith's connection with love and works — Reformed: inseparable
source_text: XXXI. Atque hactenus de fidei subjecto. Superest paucis exponendum, quid Scholae, tum Reformatae, tum Romanae Doctores sentiant circa connexionem fidei cum dilectione & bonis operibus. Et quidem Reformatorum concors sententia est veram & salvificam fidem esse a charitate penitus inseparabilem: ita ut vera fides in eo esse non possit qui charitatem non habet, & in quo Dei & proximi dilectio non reperitur. Quia scilicet ea est verae fidei indoles, ut charitatem & virtutes caeteras in anima fidelis necessario gignat, quemadmodum lux solis sine calore non est, sed perpetuo illum comitem habet.
pass_a_gloss: And so far concerning faith's subject. It remains to set out briefly what Doctors of the Reformed and Roman schools think about the connection of faith with love and good works. And indeed the concordant opinion of the Reformers is that true and saving faith is utterly inseparable from charity: so that true faith cannot be in one who does not have charity, and in whom love of God and neighbor is not found. Because such is the character of true faith that it necessarily begets charity and the other virtues in the believer's soul, just as the sun's light is not without heat, but continually has it as companion.
pass_b_english: Shift: connection of faith with love and good works.
Reformed consensus: true saving faith is inseparable from charity — light never without heat.

choices.why: True faith's nature to beget love.
